# Provider and stream boundary experiments use pinned bodies with controlled runtime mocks

Observed execution on 2026-10-13T06:55:28.662Z: Node v26.3.1,
darwin arm64. Loaded exact pinned source with vm.SourceTextModule and supplied
controlled cal, ChromeUtils, service/interface mocks and Node ReadableStream.
These are boundary experiments, not Thunderbird/Gecko product tests. Private
scripts and raw output remain outside the shared repository.

| Controlled input | Observed result | Supported scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| disabled synchronize, then enabled synchronize on the same facade | completed mPendingSync remained set; enabled operation starts=0 | assignment/early-return ordering in the exact facade body |
| online delete, normal item flag, generic non-network remote failure | facade delete promise resolved | catch branch has no rethrow for that error |
| provider invokes error modify callback, then rejects its promise | completion callback calls=2 | callback/rejection bridge has no once guard in this input |
| consume one generic stream to exhaustion through Calendar iterator | stream.locked=true | custom iterator has no releaseLock on done |
| bounded max=1, enqueue two items, explicitly close | output=["one"]; second-close TypeError | bounded close flag differs from native close state |

The mocks use actual journal flag constants CREATED=1, MODIFIED=2, DELETED=4.
The tested branches do not establish native network errors, XPIDL conversions,
UI event ordering, garbage collection, every provider callback contract, or
Gecko implementation identity. Corresponding callers/native bodies were read
separately. Node's TypeError text is not asserted to be Gecko's error text.

Exact source SHA-256 values:

- `calendar/base/src/CalCachedCalendar.sys.mjs`: `390a94aee68cff5aa4d2d40d55c9342ff332da3b6eaf869967481bcf60eb7d42`.
- `calendar/base/src/CalReadableStreamFactory.sys.mjs`: `980e0bdaf20e3afb339c0785088688512fa5133d389a315ccfdf41268853dce0`.
- `calendar/base/modules/utils/calIteratorUtils.sys.mjs`: `6c797ae64262dfad6a7748a71b02058bc2fe450ed57ae12c8aa479cfd9f7d32f`.

These results add runtime evidence for the scoped control flow. They do not
upgrade automated relationships or untested application scenarios into proven
product behavior. No production patch was made from these findings.

## Source scope

Thunderbird: `87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799`. Firefox: `1a097ed8d31f6b307a5d0ebc34a82ceaf7f3727b`. All source ranges refer to these commits.
Use `git show REVISION:repository-relative-path` in the named repository.
This is checked static behavior in the stated scope. Test links describe the
assertions read. They do not establish a passing run. Runtime experiments and
test-run limits are recorded separately. No instructions or product code changed.
